titleStmt.title: Action Memorandum From the Assistant Secretary of State for Inter-American Affairs (Abrams) to the Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs (Armacost)

div.head: 409. Action Memorandum From the Assistant Secretary of State for Inter-American Affairs (Abrams) to the Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs (Armacost)

list.label: SUBJECT
list.item: Request to Call In Paraguayan Ambassador

div.p: Although you earlier declined to meet with the Paraguayan Ambassador after the teargassing of Ambassador Taylor, I feel that the GOP’s inadequate—and even insulting—diplomatic note of explanation warrants your doing so now.

On February 18 we received the GOP’s formal response to our protest note over the incident. It is inadequate in both tone and substance. In essence, it says Ambassador Taylor is lying, accuses him of interference in Paraguay’s affairs, and does not provide the apology we asked for, or the guarantee for Americans’ safety.

The GOP insists upon trying to separate its treatment of Ambassador Taylor from its bilateral relations with the USG. By raising this with Ambassador Martinez, you would confirm the seriousness of the incident and our demand that Ambassador Taylor—and the government which he represents—be treated with deference and respect.
That you agree to call in Ambassador Martinez.

note.p: Source: Department of State, Executive Secretariat, S/S Records, 1987 Nodis and Exdis Memorandums, Lot 94D432, Nodis Memorandums February 1987. Confidential. Drafted on February 19 by Bolton; cleared by Gelbard and Howard. A stamped notation at the top of the page indicates that Armacost saw the memorandum on February 24.

Attached but not printed is telegram 48182 to Asuncion, February 19, in which the Department transmitted a translation of the Paraguayan response given by Martínez to Gelbard on February 18 to the U.S. protest of Taylor’s teargassing. The Department, noting that it was “dissatisfied with both the tone and substance of this response,” asked the Embassy for its analysis and recommendations. Also attached but not printed is telegram 695 from Asuncion, February 19, in which the Embassy provided an analysis of the Paraguayan response, characterizing it as “clearly unacceptable because it denies the facts as we witnessed them.”

Armacost indicated his approval by writing his initials. A stamped notation indicated that he did so on February 24. An unknown hand wrote “Feb 25” and “11:00” on the “Date” and “Time” lines, respectively. In telegram 58055 to Asuncion, February 28, the Department noted that on February 25 Armacost had called in Martínez “to emphasize USG’s disappointment “with the GOP’s response to our diplomatic note” on the teargassing incident. (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D870157–0247) In telegram 98136 to Asuncion, April 2, the Department reported that in an April 1 meeting with Gelbard, Martínez had presented an “acceptable” clarifying note on Paraguay’s original note; in turn, Gelbard gave Martínez a note on U.S. “satisfaction, particularly with regard to the expressions of regret and assurances concerning the personal security of Ambassador Taylor.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D870254–0865)
